newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam says can't afford to join coffee group now.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says can't afford to join coffee group now.

text.p: Vietnam is considering joining the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC), but cannot afford to do so at present, the chairman of the Vietnam Coffee and Cocoa Association said on Tuesday
Doan Trieu Nhan said Vietnam would face financial difficulties in meeting the ACPC's coffee retention plan.

"Vietnam is considering joining the ACPC... but Vietnam doesn't yet have a government coffee authority in charge of production as in other countries. We're also not financially capable of joining the ACPC retention plan," he said.
An industry official, who declined to be named, said that while Hanoi had indicated support for the ACPC it was unlikely to be ready to join for several years.
He said the conditions were not yet right, nor was there sufficient recognition in Vietnam of the need to join the international coffee group.
The Ivorian Minister for Commodities, Guy-Alain Gauze, said in an interview on Monday that he had received a pledge from Hanoi to consider at government level joining the ACPC.
Gauze visited Vietnam last week to attend a coffee conference and flew to Hanoi for talks with government officials.
Vietnam is the second largest producer of robusta coffee in Asia, but the government is seen lacking the necessary funds to afford the cost of a retention scheme.
